- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — adjust downward bias by +2–5% of recent mean.
- When sentiment turns sharply negative (e.g., -0.3 or below), reduce forecast by 3–8% to account for mean reversion or policy tightening.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings — if sentiment shifts >0.5 in 3–5 days, don’t extrapolate beyond 1–2 days unless confirmed by price action.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong downward momentum + negative sentiment, cap forecast decline at 10% below recent low.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is trending down, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day to avoid “sentiment-overfitting”.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7), use 50% of sentiment weight in price adjustment — don’t fully trust sentiment for direction.
